title: Montgrand family responds to PA shooting
subtitle: Last month's police shooting in Prince Albert is hitting very close to home for another Saskatchewan fami...
article: Last month's police shooting in Prince Albert is hitting very close to home for another Saskatchewan family.

In 2008, Jacqueline Marie Montgrand was shot by a member of the Prince Albert Police Service. Much like Ryan Natomagan, Montgrand too was carrying a knife at the time of the incident and would succumb to her injuries in hospital.
"It's sad how lives are taken by people that serve and protect. It just seems like a fail there," said Myra Laprise, Montgrand's niece.

The inquiry into the Montgrand death determined that officers were unable to escape the confrontation with the armed woman, and one officer fired his weapon. Five years after the initial incident the Montgrand family continues to seek closure.
"We're still struggling with it because it's just so remarkable and unbelievable. We still wish that she was here with us, so there's still a lot of pain and [no] closure," said Laprise.
To this day Laprise said she cannot understand why police were not able to safely take down her aunt.
"There is a whole team of them that can stop one human being with a little, small knife," she said.
She added she would like to extend her support and love to the family of Ryan Natomagan.
The investigation into the most recent police shooting is still ongoing.
At the time of the incident, police said they had responded to a domestic disturbance. Two officers had attended the scene and would fire multiple shots.
